article.story: NEW ORLEANS -- — Chuba Hubbard made long gains out of short passes, pushed through tacklers and pulled the mistake-prone Carolina Panthers out of a three-game slide. Hubbard gained 172 yards from scrimmage and ran for two touchdowns, and Ryan Fitzgerald's 54-yard field goal as time expired lifted Carolina to a 20-17 victory over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday with the NFC South Division lead at stake. “These are the moments I work hard for,” Hubbard said. “I was telling myself before every play to breathe, focus and explode. I was telling myself to remain calm, and when the play comes, just make it.” The winning kick came after Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry was called for a 30-yard pass interference penalty that gave Carolina the ball on the New Orleans 36-yard line with 21 seconds left. Hubbard rushed for 92 yards on 27 carries, and also gained 80 yards on five catches for Carolina (4-5), which won despite committing a franchise-record 17 penalties for 152 yards. The Saints (3-6) by contrast, were flagged just three times, but the last cost them the game less than 30 seconds after Charlie Smyth had hit a 55-yard field goal to tie it at 17. Saints coach Kellen Moore withheld criticism of the officials, noting that the Saints, on balance, benefitted from penalty calls. “We had plenty of opportunities in this game," Moore said. “We didn’t get it done.” While both teams entered the game with losing records, the winner was going to take the lead of their anemic division, which Carolina won in 2025 with an 8-9 record. “It was a championship opportunity,” Carolina coach Dave Canales said, only half-kidding. “We talked about that a little bit lightheartedly, and it gave the guys a chuckle, but it’s true. We have to take advantage of these moments in the division.” Carolina, which led 7-0 at halftime, was up just 10-7 when Alvin Kamara's 4-yard touchdown catch gave New Orleans a 14-10 lead with 3:49 left. Bryce Young responded with short passes to Hubbard for gains of 29 and 34 yards to set up the work-horse running back's second short TD run, putting Carolina back in front with 1:49 left. “He’s the heart and soul of everything we do,” Young said of Hubbard. “I just wanted to get it into a special player’s hands.” Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, who was intercepted and lost a fumble during the game, drove New Orleans into position for Smyth's tying field goal with 41 seconds left. Young finished 17 of 30 passing for 200 yards without a turnover. Shough was 25 of 35 for 187 yards. Saints rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson caught 11 passes for 80 yards. But the Saints struggled to run the ball despite the return of Tavis Etienne from injured reserve. Etienne gained just 14 yards on eight carries and New Orleans finished with just 49 yards rushing. Kamara scored both Saints touchdowns, the first on a 3-yard run. The loss, Shough said, “feels awful.” “It is a missed opportunity. We’ve got to beat those guys,” Shough said. “That wasn’t a win by them. Obviously, they’re a good team, but we feel like we lost that game. … We shot ourselves in the foot there and that stings even more.” Carolina is concerned about penalties Carolina's penalties included two which set up a Saints fourth-quarter TD: a 15-yard horse-collar penalty on what should have been a sack by Jaelan Phillips, followed by a 17-yard, defensive pass interference penalty on Corey Thornton that was enforced at the Carolina 2. “That’s something we’ll be talking about for sure,” Canales said. “When the margins get tighter, it makes it really hard to win that way. We have to fix that. That’s not going to be sustainable.” Both teams squandered first-half scoring chances The Saints' first possession ended with Shough's deflected, fourth-down pass being intercepted by Devin Lloyd inside the Carolina 40 and returned to the New Orleans 23. Young was then stopped short by Carl Granderson on fourth-and-2 from the Saints 3. In the second quarter, Fitzgerald missed a 48-yard field goal, keeping the game scoreless. The Saints then marched to the Carolina 35, only to have Shough lose a fumble on a failed handoff. After Carolina finally broke through on Hubbard's 2-yard touchdown run, the Saints drove to the Panthers 25, only to come up empty again when Audric Estime was stopped on fourth-and-1. “It was a lack of execution in some of those critical moments as players," Shough said. “You can’t come out of the first half with no points.” Injuries Panthers: Running back Jonathon Brooks (groin), offensive lineman Brady Christensen (hamstring) and safety Mike Jackson (groin) were not activated off injured reserve despite their recent returns to practice. Saints: Linebacker Pete Werner left the game in the first half with a hamstring injury. Up next Panthers: Host Baltimore next Sunday.
